description:
FILED s470bn (Opus, 2026-09-05), found building the `textproc` macro row.

REPRODUCER:
    use Text::Wrap qw(wrap);
    $Text::Wrap::columns = 40;
    print wrap('', '  ', join(' ', map { "word$_" } 1..40)), "\n";
  perl: wraps.  PCL: dies
    This shouldn't happen at .../5.40.3/Text/Wrap.pm line 78.

Wrap.pm:78 is inside the main `while` loop's `else` branch â the one it reaches
when none of its three regex alternatives matched the remaining text, i.e. a
regex in Wrap.pm answers differently under PCL.  The module is core and pure
perl, so this is a PCL regex or `pos`/`substr` divergence with a small
reproducer waiting inside it: bisect Wrap.pm's own three matches
(`\G([^\n]{0,$ll})($lbrk|\z)`, the greedy `\G([^\n]{$ll})`, and the
`\G([^\n]*)` tail) against perl on the same input.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE BENCH: `textproc` wraps by hand instead (the plan named
Text::Wrap as the example, not the requirement).
subject: Text::Wrap::wrap dies "This shouldn't happen" at Wrap.pm:78 under PCL
